faqs.q: Sec. 102-40. - Property owners responsible for charges.
faqs.a:
(a)
Generally.
Owners of properties are responsible for payment of all system development charges,
               assessments, costs of materials, and other fees and user charges set forth in this
               article. All billing to users may be by address only, and the fact that the person
               receiving the service may not be identified thereon by name does not preclude collection
               of the charge from the owner. The property owner shall be responsible for all utility
               administrative charges assessed pursuant to
section 102-37
.
(b)
Suspension of water service.
Subject to the provisions of this subsection (b), water service may be shut off by
               the city any time that water or sewer fees, rates, charges, or penalties are not paid
               or for any other violations of this article.
(1)
Shut off notice.
If a property owner fails to pay any water or sewer fee, rate, charge, or penalty,
               or otherwise violates this article, the city will send to the property owner a notice
               that the city may shut off water because of the non-payment or violation. The notice
               must be sent to the property owner no later than 14 calendar days prior to the date
               water service may be shut off. The notice must include the following information:
i.
If the property owner has failed to pay any water or sewer fee, rate, charge, or penalty,
               the amount of the past due payment and the date and time that payment must be properly
               received by the city to avoid suspension of service;
ii.
If the property owner has violated any other provision of this article, a description
               of the violation and the date and time by which the violation must be cured to avoid
               suspension of service;
iii.
Any additional fees the property owner may be responsible for under this section or
section 102-37
of this article;
iv.
A statement that if any water or sewer fee, rate, charge, or penalty remains unpaid
               or any other violation of this article remains uncured as of the shut off date and
               time, water service may be shut off after that date and time;
v.
Notice that under
section 18-525
of this Code, disconnection from a public water system, an approved private water
               system, or well is a violation of this Code and the property owner may be subject
               to additional enforcement mechanisms permitted by this Code including but not limited
               to posting the property as being uninhabitable; and
vi.
Notice that if the property owner does not believe reasonable cause exists for the
               suspension of service, the property owner may, no later than seven calendar days after
               the date of the notice, submit to the director a water shut off review request form.
(2)
Submitting a water shut off review request.
A property owner may, within seven days of the date of the shut off notice, submit
               to the director a water shut off review request form on a form prescribed by the city
               and available from the director on the city's website or by hard copy, setting forth
               the property owner's explanation as to why reasonable cause does not exist for the
               suspension of service. Compliance with the seven-day time limit noted in this subsection
               (2) is a jurisdictional prerequisite to any appeal brought under this section. Failure
               to comply bars the director's review of the request and any subsequent appeal by the
               property owner.
(3)
Director's review of request.
The director will, within seven days of the date of the submission of a completed
               water shut off review request form in accordance with subsections (2) and (7) of this
               section, determine whether there exists reasonable cause for the suspension of water
               service. In making this determination, the director may review the property owner's
               submission and any relevant city documents. The director will provide the property
               owner with a written determination stating whether and why reasonable cause exists
               for the suspension of water service. The decision may be mailed by first class U.S.
               Mail or furnished to the property owner electronically. Failure by the director to
               issue a written decision within seven days will be considered a denial of the property
               owner's request.
(4)
Submitting an appeal.
A property owner may appeal to the city manager the director's denial of the property
               owner's assertion that reasonable cause does not exist for water service to be shut
               off. The appeal must be submitted by the property owner within seven days of the date
               of the director's written decision, or in the event no written decision is issued
               by the director, within 14 days of the date the property owner submitted the request
               for review, and must be submitted on a form prescribed by the city and available from
               the director on the city's website or by hard copy. The appeal must be submitted to
               the city clerk in accordance with subsection (7) of this section. Compliance with
               the seven-day or, if applicable, fourteen-day time limit noted in this subsection
               (4) is a jurisdictional prerequisite to any appeal brought under this article. Failure
               to comply bars the appeal.
(5)
City manager's review of appeal.
The city manager will, within 14 days of the date of submission of a completed appeal
               form, determine whether there exists reasonable cause for the suspension of water
               service. In making this determination, the city manager may review the property owner's
               submission and any relevant city documents. The city manager will provide the property
               owner with a written determination stating whether and why reasonable cause exists
               for the suspension of water service. The decision may be mailed by first class U.S.
               Mail or furnished to the property owner electronically. Failure by the city manager
               to issue a written decision on the appeal within the time frame set forth in this
               subsection, will be considered a denial of the property owner's appeal and the property
               owner may proceed as if an adverse decision has been issued.
(6)
Appeal of city manager's decision.
The city manager's decision, or denial of an appeal as a result of the city manager's
               failure to issue a written decision, shall be considered a final agency decision.
               The appeal may proceed under Rule 106 of the Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure.
(7)
Complete forms required.
A water shut off review request form or an appeal form that is not complete in all
               respects shall be promptly returned to the property owner and will not be submitted
               to the director or the city manager, as applicable, for review. The property owner
               may resubmit a water shut off review request form or an appeal form deemed incomplete,
               and the city shall accept it, if the resubmitted form is complete and submitted within
               the seven-day or 14-day, as applicable, time limits set forth in this section for
               submitting a water shut off review request form or an appeal form.
(8)
Suspension of service not tolled during appeal process.
Suspension of service will not be tolled during any active appeals process brought
               pursuant to subsection (4), (5), or (6) of this section, including the time periods
               that a property owner may submit an appeal, if the past due water or sewer fees, rates,
               charges, or penalties remain unpaid or the violation remains uncured. If a property
               owner pays their balance in full to restore service during an appeal and receives
               a decision in their favor from the appeal, then any amount deemed to have been paid
               in error as a result of the appeal decision will be promptly credited to the property
               owner.
(9)
Restoration of service.
The city will restore water service when the balance is paid in full, including any
               restoration of service fees or other applicable fees and charges, when a violation
               is cured, upon a decision in favor of the property owner by the city manager of a
               property owner's appeal, or upon a decision in favor of the property owner in an appeal
               of the city manager's decision. The city will only restore water service during the
               city's regular business hours.
(10)
Fees.
The city may assess service charges, delinquent charges, and any other fee or charge
               it deems appropriate. The property owner is responsible for paying any charges or
               fees assessed pursuant to this section. Notwithstanding anything in this Code to the
               contrary, the director may reduce or waive any amount assessed if the director determines
               there are significant extenuating circumstances. The director will establish a policy
               for evaluating claims of significant extenuating circumstance for purposes of this
               subsection.
